prelaunch_freshness: Before launch, preserve the complete prior controller result, three phase results, checkpoint, and their exact bytes/hashes/run IDs when present.

With no valid active checkpoint, the controller first requires kernel READY with TARGET_NONE, then truncates and verifies the current result and all phase paths before writing schema vitacheat.foreign-target-gate.result.v4 with build_id VCFG-RESULT-V4.
An exact preserved prior result is stale waiting evidence, not an anomaly. Ignore it until an empty observation or a complete current-identity document appears.

A complete phase result is fresh only when schema/build/title/firmware/scope match, result_cleared is true, run_id is nonzero, and transaction/previous-run/phase/index/offset metadata exactly forms the three-run chain.

The 96-byte checkpoint is valid only with exact magic/version/size/integrity, zero reserved fields, distinct run IDs, monotonic counters, and a permitted phase transition. Zero bytes means no active transaction. Wait states 1/2 are resumable exactly once; launch-pending/running states 3-6 are preserved incomplete-transaction blockers; any malformed/partial checkpoint also stops without truncation.
Preserve partial current writes and poll read-only. Reject a structurally complete malformed/current-identity mismatch; never infer tests from a partial document.
Before each generation the controller truncates and verifies zero bytes at ux0:data/vitacheat-foreign-target-layout.bin.
Before each generation the controller truncates and verifies zero bytes at ux0:data/vitacheat-foreign-target-startup.bin.
Before each generation the controller truncates and verifies zero bytes at ux0:data/vitacheat-foreign-target-fixture.json.
Any cleanup/open/close/readback failure is recorded and stops before launch.
run: Preserve the prior current/phase results and checkpoint before launch. During polling, treat exact preserved bytes as stale waiting evidence rather than a test-order failure.

Require phase 1 schema-v4 tests 1-8 at offset 0 with exact build/schema/transaction/run identity and passing clear-controller-result; preserve its pre-target status-v2 baseline, then allow the controller to verify target-unavailable, clear the three target evidence paths, persist the phase-1 checkpoint, and launch VCFT00001.
Poll the startup-stage path read-only. Preserve every distinct invalid/partial byte sequence and continue polling without input.

Require one complete valid v2 prompt-ready record with exact build/title/schema identity, sentinel result 0, wrong-caller last result -12, readiness probe result 0, exactly one attempt, bounded elapsed time, layout result 0, and fixture result 0. Any delayed -13 to -12 transition contradicts create-before-user-entry and stops before input.
Require the exact 32-byte layout and complete fixture JSON independently; the startup record alone is never target-start or read authority.
Send exactly one documented bounded input: press cross; wait 100ms; release cross.

After the first X, require a distinct controller run with phase 2 tests 9-28 at offset 8 and the exact transaction/previous-run chain. Generation 1 must show exactly one target-create match/authorization delta, at least one create callback delta, either zero start callbacks/revalidations or at least 19 successful same-PID start revalidations, and zero saturation.

Allow phase 2 to require kernel TARGET_STARTED, read, destroy only VCFT00001, prove the exact exit lifecycle stage, verify the stale handle, clear all three target evidence paths, and relaunch VCFT00001.

Repeat the prompt-ready validation and one bounded X input for generation 2. Require a third distinct controller run with phase 3 tests 29-35 at offset 28 and the same permitted generation profile from the generation-1-exit baseline.

Require old-handle rejection, a distinct new handle, exact 64-byte relaunch read, close, zero-byte completed checkpoint, and exact concatenation of all three phase arrays into the canonical 35-test order.
Retrieve current and all phase controller JSON files, checkpoint bytes, fixture JSON, startup records/partials, layouts, and all available serial lines beginning VCFG.
